name: Theophilus
overview: Theophilus is a male figure identified as the recipient or audience of the Gospel of Luke, as stated in Luke 1:3. Beyond this unique role, Scripture does not provide details about his tribe or other personal notes. His primary significance lies in being the addressed individual for Luke's detailed account of the life and ministry of Jesus Christ.
namesAndTitles: Theophilus is the only recorded name for this individual, and no specific meaning or title is provided in the biblical text. The name is simply presented as a proper name in Luke 1:3 without additional explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Theophilus beyond his identification as the recipient of Luke's account. No other personal or relational details are given.
scriptureSignificance: Theophilus serves as the named audience for the Gospel of Luke, indicating the personal and intentional nature of Luke's narrative. His mention highlights the evangelistic and instructive purpose of the Gospel, aiming to provide a reliable and orderly account of Jesus Christ's life and teachings. Through addressing Theophilus, Luke emphasizes the importance of faith grounded in eyewitness testimony and careful investigation.
